versions.research_rationale: EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Savings: EO 10577's proviso carried the schedule listings into the new rules.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10577 sec. 301 attaches a proviso to its revocations: positions listed in Schedules A, B and C 'as provided for in Civil Service Rule VI of that order, as amended' (that is, Rule VI as rewritten by EO 10440, which created Schedule C) 'shall be considered as being listed in Schedules A, B, and C, respectively,' of the new Rule VI, unless and until the Commission removes them. The Commission's schedule placements made under EO 10440 were therefore carried into EO 10577's schedules; they continue, if at all, under EO 10577 and later rules, not under EO 10440. No other savings clause was found.
